messages:
sam: Hey team — I opened a PR that touches both frontend/components/button and infra/deploy/k8s. Not sure who can approve this since CODEOWNERS lists different teams. link: https://git.redwood.ai/pr/5621

alex: If it touches infra/deploy it will require an infra owner approval. CODEOWNERS is pretty strict on path-based rules. Did you split the change?

maria: quick q — is the infra change just a namespace label tweak? if it's tiny we sometimes allow eng-platform to approve but only with an explicit opt-in.

sam: It's two small things: a prop rename in button and a one-line label in k8s/service.yaml. I tried to split but the service label references the new prop name for telemetry routing.

nate: tl;dr: per policy, any file under /infra/* needs an infra-team approval. We can do a one-off exception if infra owners ok it, but prefer split PRs for clearer audit trail.

liz: I'm on infra rotation this week. I can review the k8s change and approve if it's just the label. ping me the exact diff. :+1:

sam: thanks @liz — diff pasted below:
```
--- a/infra/deploy/service.yaml
+++ b/infra/deploy/service.yaml
@@ -12,7 +12,7 @@
 metadata:
-  labels:
-    app: old-button
+  labels:
+    app: new-button-prop
 spec:
   selector:
     matchLabels:
@@ -45,6 +45,7 @@
 spec:
   template:
     metadata:
+      annotations:
       labels:
         component: frontend
 ```

alex: dev-bot CI shows required reviewers: @infra-team missing. dev-bot: `check: required approvers not satisfied`

dev-bot: CI / required-approvals check failed — missing approvers from: @infra-team. See: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/5621/checks

maria: @liz if you can +1 on infra, I'll do the frontend review and we can get this merged in one PR. Otherwise I'll split and re-open a frontend-only PR.

liz: OK I'll take a look in ~30m. if it's purely label/annotation then i'll approve. FYI we prefer splitting but this is fine for a small correction.

sam: thanks — tagging eng-platform in case we want a short-term guidance doc on cross-area tiny fixes and who can approve. maybe we need an explicit CODEOWNERS override process.

nate: agree we should document. short-term: infra owners approve, frontend owners approve — if both +1 then merge. long-term: we'll add a PR template question: "Does this touch infra?" and suggest splitting.

merge-bot: auto-merge blocked — required reviewers pending. will attempt merge after all required approvals are present.
